{"at": "2026-10-17T14:58:28.326054+00:00", "source": "Exact current work_items:get results; initial batch read budgets exhausted for 71 rows, recovered in <=20-id batches.", "records": {"EI-21273488869953924": {"id": "EI-21273488869953924", "ok": true, "availability": "available", "error": null, "workItem": {"id": "EI-21273488869953924", "kind": "bug", "family": "issue", "harness": "papercusp", "title": "papercusp-su MCP client wedges session-wide with 'superuser_invalid_bearer' while the credential, proxy and operator are all healthy \u2014 agents wrongly conclude they are blocked", "summary": "SYMPTOM\nEvery papercusp-su tool call in a live session began returning `request_rejected: superuser_invalid_bearer` \u2014 reads and writes alike (loop:status rejects identically to loop:checkpoint), so it is not tool-specific. It persisted ~10min across two turns and cost one full turn's checkpoint (three loop:checkpoint attempts refused; a whole turn's findings were nearly stranded).\n\nTHE ERROR NAMES THE WRONG SUBJECT \u2014 falsified directly\n'superuser_invalid_bearer' is a claim about a CREDENTIAL, so it sends you to token rotation / operator restart. Both are red herrings. Measured with curl while the in-process surface was still rejecting:\n - bearer read from ~/.claude.json -> HTTP 200 + full tools/list on :9071 (proxy), :3070 (operator) AND :3170 (staging).\n - tools/call loop:status with that SAME bearer AND the session's OWN SID (su-c1dea4c8-...) -> {\"ok\":true,\"ownerId\":\"su-c1dea4c8-...\"}. The exact call that had just been rejected in-process SUCCEEDED over HTTP.\nSo: token valid, proxy healthy, operator healthy, session/client binding accepted. The ONLY broken component is Claude Code's in-process MCP client, which the error message never mentions.\n\nNOT RESOURCE EXHAUSTION (checked before blaming load)\nMeasured at 19:28Z during the outage: load 62.58/128 cores (~49%), 195G/251G memory used with 55G available, PSI memory full avg10=0.02. Nothing saturated. Do not misfile this as load pressure.\n\nCONTEXT: papercup-staging-api re-entered active at 15:17:02 EDT (19:17Z), ~7min before the first rejection, and the turn logged the papercusp-su MCP server disconnecting mid-turn. Correlation only \u2014 NOT asserted as cause, since the post-restart credential demonstrably works.\n\nWHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN ONE OUTAGE\nA wedged client is not loss of capability, but it is indistinguishable from one at the call site. An agent that trusts the message concludes the platform is down and either idles or ends its turn \u2014 a fleet LEADER doing so stops monitoring its whole fleet. That is the real cost.\n\nWORKAROUND THAT FULLY RESTORES THE SURFACE\nThe tools are plain HTTP behind a bearer in ~/.claude.json, so a ~40-line bridge recovers ALL of them:\n  python3 /tmp/pcsu/call.py <tool:name> <args.json>\nPOST to $PAPERCUSP_OPERATOR_URL/api/mcp?superuser=1&client=$PAPERCUSP_SID with Authorization: Bearer <token from ~/.claude.json>, Accept: application/json, text/event-stream; parse the SSE `data: ` line. The loop:checkpoint that had failed three times was written through it (verified:true, contentHash ff6dc98152e4).\n\nASKS\n1. Make the error distinguish a client-session fault from a rejected credential \u2014 the current wording reliably sends agents to the wrong subsystem.\n2. Have the client re-handshake instead of rejecting every call indefinitely.\n3. Consider shipping the HTTP bridge as a supported fallback so agents stop re-deriving it.\n\nRELATED (same family, less precisely diagnosed): EI-9452, EI-19285078178745571.", "state": "done", "assignee": null, "takenAt": null, "lastProgressAt": null, "assignedBy": null, "createdBy": "su-c1dea4c8-7b9a-419f-bccb-a4a83e215ba9", "severity": "major", "goalId": null, "tags": null, "sourcePlanSlug": null, "sourcePlanItemIds": null, "redundancy": null, "expectedCostCents": null, "parent": null, "payload": {"_ei": {"scope": "harness:papercusp", "source": "su", "severity": "major", "created_by": "su-c1dea4c8-7b9a-419f-bccb-a4a83e215ba9", "assigned_by": null, "found_during": null, "linked_feature_id": null}, "filedByRole": "su", "watchdogKey": "repeated-tool-error:loop:checkpoint:structural:request-rejected-superuser-invalid-bearer-returned", "_assumptions": {"declared": "none", "resolvedAt": "2026-08-24T05:38:59.650Z"}, "dedupCoverage": {"lexical": "ok", "degraded": true, "semantic": "unavailable"}, "ideaLifecycle": {"state": "open", "stateUpdatedAt": "2026-08-23T19:32:59.950Z"}, "admissionIdentity": {"titleKey": "title:agents all and are bearer blocked client conclude credential healthy invalid mcp operator papercusp proxy session superuser the they wedges while wide with wrongly", "signalKey": "repeated-tool-error:loop:checkpoint:structural:request-rejected-superuser-invalid-bearer-returned", "schemaVersion": "admission-identity-v1"}, "freshnessEnvelope": {"observedAt": "2026-08-23T19:32:59.950Z", "linkedFixRefs": [], "reporterSession": "su-c1dea4c8-7b9a-419f-bccb-a4a83e215ba9", "observedSourceSha": "a2d69cef50", "observedRuntimeSha": "a2d69cef50", "deployBuildIdentity": "a2d69cef50@0.0.0", "reporterRuntimeVersion": "0.0.0", "lastSuccessfulReproductionAt": "2026-08-23T19:32:59.950Z"}, "_completionEvidence": {"summary": "Current-HEAD validation does not reproduce the reported session-wide superuser_invalid_bearer wedge. Make the Android app pair with and fully operate against that cloud workspace with no LAN: QR/manual pairing from the cloud workspace, token storage/rotation/revocation, endpoint discovery and reconnection, workspace/harness scope, sync, chat streaming, approvals, monitoring, voice and push. Model per D-013: opaque base URL with the portal relay prefix; portal device-http relay plane; auth stays on the VM; workspace_offline is its own error. Voice and turn bodies above the 512 KiB relay frame cap are chunked. A relay refusal (403) must not force a re-pair. Bar: R-13. 'The backup file exists' is not 'the backup works' \u2014 only its FRESHNESS discriminates.\n\nLIKELY CAUSES (check in this order):\n 1. db-backup.sh's timer stopped firing: systemctl --user status papercusp-db-backup.timer papercusp-db-backup.service ; journalctl --user -u papercusp-db-backup.service -n 50. Vendor docs describe capabilities and responsibilities, not an independent audit. OpenAI endpoint retention varies and ZDR has eligibility/feature limits; Salesforce documents masking disabled for agents; AWS leaves session-user mapping to the application. Report has full citations and caveats.\n\n## Key insight\nEnterprise patterns converge on a governed workload model: unique agent identity + human/delegated identity; policy enforcement before retrieval; typed action broker outside the model; isolated runtime and restricted egress; secrets broker; explicit provider/region/retention policy; immutable audit/revocation.
